5.3.142: Like an old tale: but it appears she lives,
5.3.143: Though yet she speak not. Mark a little while.
5.3.144: Please you to interpose, fair madam: kneel
5.3.145: And pray your mother’s blessing. Turn, good lady;
5.3.148: And from your sacred vials pour your graces
5.3.149: Upon my daughter’s head! Tell me, mine own.
5.3.150: Where hast thou been preserved? where lived? how found
5.3.151: Thy father’s court? for thou shalt hear that I,
5.3.152: Knowing by Paulina that the oracle
5.3.153: Gave hope thou wast in being, have preserved
5.3.156: Lest they desire upon this push to trouble
5.3.157: Your joys with like relation. Go together,
5.3.158: You precious winners all; your exultation
5.3.159: Partake to every one. I, an old turtle,
5.3.160: Will wing me to some wither’d bough and there
5.3.161: My mate, that’s never to be found again,
5.3.164: Thou shouldst a husband take by my consent,
5.3.165: As I by thine a wife: this is a match,
5.3.166: And made between’s by vows. Thou hast found mine;
5.3.167: But how, is to be question’d; for I saw her,
5.3.168: As I thought, dead, and have in vain said many
5.3.169: A prayer upon her grave. I’ll not seek far—
5.3.170: For him, I partly know his mind—to find thee
5.3.172: And take her by the hand, whose worth and honesty
5.3.173: Is richly noted and here justified
5.3.174: By us, a pair of kings. Let’s from this place.
5.3.175: What! look upon my brother: both your pardons,
5.3.176: That e’er I put between your holy looks
5.3.177: My ill suspicion. This is your son-in-law,
5.3.178: And son unto the king, who, heavens directing,
5.3.179: Is troth-plight to your daughter. Good Paulina,
5.3.180: Lead us from hence, where we may leisurely
5.3.181: Each one demand an answer to his part
5.3.182: Perform’d in this wide gap of time since first
5.3.183: We were dissever’d: hastily lead away.
